scientific_question: Can an online-selected root-only Sequential Halving schedule improve Silver gameplay without changing survivor scoring, internal search, chance search, or the leaf evaluator?

hypotheses.h0: No schedule improves independent paired gameplay over ordinary UCT at the same total root budget.
hypotheses.h1: A gentler reduction shape or more cautious early allocation preserves the exploratory gameplay benefit while reducing premature elimination.
hypotheses.h2: Any apparent screening gain disappears on fresh confirmation seeds.

stages.arms: ordinary c=25 plus all 4x3 shape/allocation treatments
stages.selection: Reject operational failures or runtime above 1.15x control; rank by paired win delta, then paired mean-floor delta, then lower runtime; promote up to the best three surviving schedules. Stop if none survive.

stages.arms: ordinary c=25 control and each of the three promoted schedules at every budget
stages.selection: Within each budget compare to its paired control. Reject operational failures, runtime above 1.10x, or paired mean-floor 95% lower bound below -2.0. Rank remaining schedule-budget pairs by paired win delta, then floor delta, then proximity to 3000 simulations.

arms: single frozen Sequential Halving schedule at c=25 internals
stages.gate: No operational failures; exact simulation divisibility; SH CPU <=1.10x c25; SH paired win delta >=5pp with 95% lower bound >0; paired mean-floor 95% lower bound >=-1.0.
stages.claim_limit: SH is promising only if the full gate passes

root_c_interaction.reason: Sequential Halving forces every root pull, so root UCT c is not consulted and c=35+SH would be an identical mislabeled arm.
root_c_interaction.comparison: ordinary c=35 remains a distinct independent-confirmation arm

stopping_rules: Stop before Stage 2 if no Stage-1 treatment survives operational/runtime checks.
Stop before Stage 3 if no Stage-2 schedule-budget pair survives safety/runtime checks.
Do not change defaults or restore general pruning when the independent gate fails.
